groups.label: (1, A)
groups.name: 1st Conjugation Group A
notes: The majority of 1st Conjugation verbs belong to this group

groups.label: (1, B)
groups.name: 1st Conjugation Group B
notes: All of the 1st Conjugation verbs with the present/future stem formant (PFSF) -ი belong to this group. Their conjugation pattern differs from that of Group A only in two forms: third person plural in the present and future tenses. In all other forms they follow the pattern of Group A.

groups.label: (1, C)
groups.name: 1st Conjugation Group C
notes: Some verbs with no vowel in their root belong to this group. They differ from the verbs in Group A only in the 3rd-person singular form of the aorist. All other forms follow the pattern of Group A.

groups.label: (1, D)
groups.name: 1st Conjugation Group D
notes: A small number of 1st Conjugation verbs produce the vowel -ა- in their root in the aorist and optative tenses in both the singular and plural. In all other ways their conjugation pattern is similar to the verbs in Group A.

groups.label: (1, E)
groups.name: 1st Conjugation Group E
notes: Some verbs of the 1st Conjugation are irregular and should be memorized individually. Most of them change their roots in the future tense, which is the base for the formation of the aorist and optative, following the pattern of Group-A.

იცი (you) know
This is a unique verb in that the subject must be in the ergative case in both the present and the imperfect. For practical purposes, its conjugation should be memorized in these two tenses. ამ კაცმო არ იცის (This man does not know). As you can see "this man" is in ergative case.
Other examples: სწავლობ, ისწავლი, ისწავლე, ისწავლო

groups.label: (2, A)
groups.name: 2nd Conjugation Group A
notes: For practical use, certain verbs are best learned only in their third-person singular form.
Doniani verbs

groups.label: (2, B)
groups.name: 2nd Conjugation Group B
notes: Iniani verbs
Verbs have  the preradical -ი, vowel in all tenses, but follow the pattern in group A. კარგია!!
The majority of these verbs are not used when referring ot a person.

groups.label: (2, C)
groups.name: 2nd Conjugation Group C
notes: Verbs of motion
Preverbs indicate the direction of movement.

There are seven basic preverbs, roughly correspoding to the English to, in, up, down, over, ect. One of the most frequently used prefixes is მი- denoting going away. The preverb მო- indicates to come here, and could be combined with each of the preverbs.

groups.label: (2, D)
groups.name: 2nd Conjugation Group D
notes: The verb be
The verb be is highly irregular with a different root in all tenses.

groups.label: (3, A)
groups.name: 3rd Conjugation Group A
notes: The majority of 3rd Conjugation verbs belong to this group. And have a PFSF of ობ

groups.label: (3, B)
groups.name: 3rd Conjugation Group B
notes: All verbs ending with -ი have thsi conjugation pattern. The suffix forming the imperfect of these verbs is not -დი but -ოდი. The conjugation patterns in the future, aorist and optative tenses are exactly the same as in group A.

groups.label: (4, A)
groups.name: 4th Conjugation Group A
notes: Subjects of these verbs are in the nominative, while direct objects are in the dative. There are about three dozen verbs of this conjugation. The third person markers in parentheses, (ჰ), and (ს), are usually dropped in the spoken forms.
